He used AI to turn his daughter's textbooks into podcasts, to help her work around dyslexia.](https://img.ksl.com/slc/3197/319734/31973413.jpg?filter=kslv2/responsive_story_lg&v=1786420416)

KEY TAKEAWAYS
- Utah teachers embrace AI in classrooms as new state guidelines take effect. - AI personalizes learning but raises concerns about accuracy and responsible use. - Educators emphasize verifying AI information and addressing potential cheating concerns.
## Making learning more accessible Stewart has seen AI's potential firsthand through his own daughter, who is dyslexic and has struggled with reading.
Using AI, he converted her textbooks into podcasts so she could listen to course materials rather than read them.
## A new skill: verifying information If AI generated an image of an orange shark, students would be encouraged to question it.
## More time for teaching AI is also creating new ways for students to engage with lessons. In one classroom demonstration, students interacted with an AI version of aviation pioneer Amelia Earhart, asking questions about her life and experiences.

item.title: As students return to school, AI takes a seat in Charleston County classrooms
item.description:
The Charleston County School District is launching a districtwide artificial intelligence policy this school year aimed at teaching students and staff how to use AI responsibly rather than trying to keep the technology out of classrooms.
District leaders said the question is no longer whether students and educators will interact with artificial intelligence, but how they can use it in a way that supports learning while protecting academic integrity.
Superintendent Anita Huggins said CCSD is among the first districts to create a comprehensive approach to artificial intelligence in schools.
Clamp said the district’s first step with artificial intelligence is building understanding among students, staff and families.
“For Charleston County School District, the integration of artificial intelligence first begins with literacy, building the background literacy of staff, of students and of families to both understand how the technology works and then more specifically how the technology will work for them,” Clamp said.
Superintendent Anita Huggins said the district’s goal is to make sure artificial intelligence supports student learning without replacing the skills students need to develop.
The district is also investing in AI tools and infrastructure, with funding already budgeted for artificial intelligence initiatives in fiscal year 2027.
As artificial intelligence continues to become more common in education and the workplace, district leaders said the goal is not to replace traditional learning, but to help students understand how to use new technology responsibly.

item.title: AI in Nebraska education: Parents, teachers and students grapple with artificial intelligence in schools
item.description:
# AI in Nebraska education: Parents, teachers and students grapple with artificial intelligence in schools #### Listen To This Story She said she found out Omaha Public Schools, where her daughter is enrolled, uses a fluency-grading AI tool called Amira.
The use of artificial intelligence is growing in classrooms, with national data showing more teachers and students are using it. According to a Center for Democracy & Technology [survey](https://cdt.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/2024-03-21-CDT-Civic-Tech-Generative-AI-Survey-Research-final.pdf), 83% of teachers reported using ChatGPT or another generative AI tool in the 2023-24 school year. Results from a Pew Research Center [survey](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/02/24/how-teens-use-and-view-ai/) showed more than half of teenagers say they used an AI chatbot to find information or get help with schoolwork.
She noticed when students were using Grammarly, an AI editing software, they weren’t learning how to properly write.
## **Ethics, inaccuracies raise questions** Jordan Martin, who will start his first year as the high school business teacher at Wilber-Clatonia Public Schools, said artificial intelligence is helping him develop some of his materials, like coming up with wrong answers for multiple-choice questions on tests.
There’s also a systemwide policy on ways faculty can [utilize](https://nebraska.edu/offices/information-technology-services/technology-support/artificial-intelligence/responsible-use#faculty) AI tools, which includes using it to “enhance or improve assignments.”
## **Avoiding artificial intelligence** “Whether it's physical medium or digital or whatever it may be, you're partaking in the act of creation.
“Someone, instead of doing the work themselves, they just typed it into ChatGPT or whatever they used and had it generate all of their looks for them,” Traxler said.

item.title: North Carolina Central University opens NC's first artificial intelligence building
item.description:
# North Carolina Central University opens NC's first artificial intelligence building There are currently 208 programs offering a bachelor's degree in Artificial Intelligence, and North Carolina Central University is the first North Carolina college to offer a dedicated AI building.
Posted
8/11/2026, 2:45:42 PM
- Related - [artificial intelligence](https://www.wral.com/tags/?tag=artificial-intelligence) artificial intelligence - North Carolina Central University - HBCUs
![NCCU ribbon cutting ](https://images.wral.com/361c61f0-6fc8-4a0a-9be8-331dbf041748?w=1200&h=675&f=jpg)NCCU ribbon cutting
By WRAL Staff
There are currently 208 programs offering a bachelor's degree in Artificial Intelligence. However, North Carolina Central University is the first North Carolina college to build a dedicated AI building, called the Institute for Artifical Intelligence and Emerging Research ( [IAIER](https://www.nccu.edu/research/institutes-and-special-facilities/iaier)).
On Monday, the college cut the ribbon on the first artifical intelligence institute established by a historically Black college or university (HBCU).
Last year the school added a module introducing AI to freshman in a mandatory university education class in the Fall. They will being offering a minor in AI through the NCCU Department of Mathematics and Physics beginning Fall 2026.
"Artifical intelligence is transforming nearly every industry," said NCCU Chancellor Karrie G. Dixon. "We want to not only prepare students but help them shape AI."
Inside features an AI Literacy Studio, Machine Learning and Data Science Studio, Robotics and Emerging Tech Lab, XR Innovation Sandbox, Ethics and Governance classrooms and Innovation Atrium.

item.title: Two public Kentucky universities launch artificial intelligence degrees this fall
item.description:
# Two public Kentucky universities launch artificial intelligence degrees this fall - [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=755367488672459&display=popup&href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.weku.org%2Fthe-commonwealth%2F2026-08-11%2Ftwo-public-kentucky-universities-launch-artificial-intelligence-degrees-this-fall) - [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.weku.org%2Fthe-commonwealth%2F2026-08-11%2Ftwo-public-kentucky-universities-launch-artificial-intelligence-degrees-this-fall&mini=true&title=Two%20public%20Kentucky%20universities%20launch%20artificial%20intelligence%20degrees%20this%20fall&summary=The%20new%20majors%20are%20part%20of%20larger%20computer%20science%20programs%20and%20come%20as%20AI%20is%20more%20widely%20adopted%20across%20many%20sectors.&source=WEKU) - [Email](mailto:?body=Two%20public%20Kentucky%20universities%20launch%20artificial%20intelligence%20degrees%20this%20fall%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.weku.org%2Fthe-commonwealth%2F2026-08-11%2Ftwo-public-kentucky-universities-launch-artificial-intelligence-degrees-this-fall%0A%0AThe%20new%20majors%20are%20part%20of%20larger%20computer%20science%20programs%20and%20come%20as%20AI%20is%20more%20widely%20adopted%20across%20many%20sectors.)
## The new majors are part of larger computer science programs and come as AI is more widely adopted across many sectors. Two Kentucky universities have launched degrees in artificial intelligence for the fall semester, responding to workforce changes and student interest as AI becomes more widely used across many sectors.
The University of Kentucky and Murray State University are adding the degrees to their selection of computer science education.
Brent Harrison, professor of computer science and the director of undergraduate studies for computer science and AI at UK, said the degree is about understanding the effects of AI and when it’s appropriate to use it.
“There's too much money, and the people that are making the decisions, like quite frankly, they don't know how the systems work, and so they make decisions, maybe optimizing for the wrong thing, and so through this degree, what I'm hoping is that again we can try we can by educating the populace, you enable them to make better decisions, put AI on a on a good path.”
![Brent Harrison is a professor of computer science and artificial intelligence at the University of Kentucky, on August 7, 2026. He said students who graduate with the new artificial intelligence degree should be able to get computer science jobs.](https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e08b494/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6000x4000+0+0/resize/880x587!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F76%2F9d%2F26b88cb1479b82137a63e111a4f5%2Fimg-3519.JPG)
Lily Burris
/
WEKU
He said students who graduate with the new artificial intelligence degree should be able to get computer science jobs.
UK’s program has about 30 students enrolled this fall, but Harrison hopes it grows to about 200.
Murray State’s program has a couple of students, but Matthew Tennyson, professor and department chair for computer science and information systems, said he also expects more interest.
“They'll choose AI rather than computer science.”
The addition of the degree programs at the two public Kentucky universities comes as businesses and individuals widely adopt AI, though critics have raised concern over the [impact of energy use and infrastructure needed](https://iee.psu.edu/news/blog/why-ai-uses-so-much-energy-and-what-we-can-do-about-it) to keep large-scale learning models operating.
The courses focus on logic and reasoning, as well as the math behind computing.
“We wanted to make sure it gelled with other engineering majors, so you could easily transfer in and out, and we wanted to make sure that again there was this foundation in computing, but this application towards AI.”
The advantage to the AI degree over the computer science degree is an advanced knowledge of application, Harrison said.
![Matthew Tennyson is the department chair of computer science and information system at Murray State University. He said the new artificial intelligence degree was created in response to workforce changes and student demand.](https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a72a8f0/2147483647/strip/true/crop/350x350+0+0/resize/880x880!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F56%2F39%2F1b62e54946379a3c58458a279434%2Fmatthew-tennyson.png)
Provided by Murray State University
Matthew Tennyson, department chair of computer science and information system at Murray State University, said the new artificial intelligence degree was created in response to workforce changes and student demand.
“In the AI degree, you have to take classes that are specific to AI, so there's an intro to AI class, an intro to machine learning class,” Tennyson said. “There's a deep learning class, and then we had to create some advanced electives in AI, as well.”
Murray State has had an undergraduate certificate program and a minor in AI, as well a data science and AI track in the computer science major.
